title: White vs Cream Paper: How It Changes Your Spine Width (KDP & IngramSpark) | SparkPrep
h1: White vs cream paper: how your paper choice changes your spine
description: Cream paper is thicker than white, so the same book needs a wider spine. See KDP and IngramSpark spine numbers by paper, and how to avoid a cover that no longer fits.
lead: Switching from white to cream paper feels like a small choice. It changes your cover size.
error: Spine width does not match the page count and paper selected
errorNote: Paraphrased. This is what you get when a cover built for white paper is uploaded for a cream-paper book.
why:
Every page adds thickness, and cream paper is thicker than white. So the same 300-page book has a different spine on each paper:

KDP paperSpine per page300 pages
White0.002252"0.676"
Cream0.0025"0.750"
Premium color0.002347"0.704"

IngramSpark measures paper in pages per inch: about 512 for white 50#, 444 for creme 50#, 400 for groundwood and 377 for 70# color. Each printer's own numbers only work for that printer.

steps: Pick your paper first, then get the cover size.
Use the spine width calculator or the printer's own template for that paper.
Get a new template for the new paper and page count.
Widen the cover by the difference, move the front panel over, and re-center the spine text.

cta.text: Changed your paper or page count? SparkPrep recalculates the spine for your printer and paper and refits your cover in minutes.

faq.q: Is cream paper thicker than white?
faq.a: Yes. On KDP a cream page adds 0.0025 inch to the spine and a white page adds 0.002252 inch, so cream books have wider spines.

faq.q: Can I use KDP's spine width for IngramSpark?
faq.a: No. Each printer's paper is different, so always use that printer's own numbers or template.
